title: Smoke or fire from your car: what to do now
h1: Smoke or fire from the car
metaDesc: Smoke or fire from your car? Pull over, turn off the engine, get everyone out, leave the hood closed, move 100 feet away and call 911.
first: If you see smoke and think your car may be on fire, pull over as soon as it's safe and turn off the engine.
Get everyone out. Leave the hood closed.
Move at least 100 feet from the car and stay away from traffic.
Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames.
dont: Don't open the hood or the trunk.
Never go back to the car for anything.
Don't try to put out the fire yourself.

steps.t: Steam from under the hood often means the engine is overheating. Pull over and turn the engine off, and never open the radiator cap while it's hot. If you're not sure whether it's steam or smoke, treat it as smoke: get everyone out and call 911.
Well away from traffic, behind a guardrail if there is one, at least 100 feet from the car.
Don't drive the car. Have it towed and checked.

call: Call 911 for any smoke or fire from the car, even if it seems to stop.

sources.t: Oregon DMV: Parent guide to teen driving, emergencies
